text:
Ravi: quick doc PR incoming — small but important clarity around quota hover text, burst credits, and how override headers affect per-token attribution. customers keep opening tickets after seeing the quota panel and thinking their whole key was reclassified. :alarm_clock:
Zoe: can you paste the exact UI copy that's confusing? happy to help reword.
Ravi: current tooltip on the quota widget says: "Usage billed at plan tier. See pricing for details." which is terse and misleading. I propose: "Billing is computed per token. Tokens inherit the API key tier by default. An optional request header can attribute tokens in this request to a different tier (see examples).");
Zoe: much clearer. Also add a short note about "burst credits" and soft limits — people think hitting a soft limit means a tier change. We should show the sequence: soft limit hit -> burst credits used -> routing fallback -> tokens still attributed to same tier unless override header changed.
Ravi: good point. Draft paragraph I'll add: "Burst credits are consumed before switching to fallback capacity. If a fallback model handles the request, billing attribution remains the same as the API key (or the explicit override header) unless you change the header/api-key. The quota panel shows remaining burst credits and a separate line for tokens attributed via override headers."
Marta: please include a compact example that shows mixed attribution inside one billing window. Also add a Rust SDK snippet — docs currently only show curl/node/python and we've been asked about Rust by a customer.
Ravi: example I'm adding:
```
Billing window 2026-12-01:
- API key tier (default): startup -> 900 tokens
- Requests with override header: pro -> 225 tokens
Result: 900 tokens billed at startup tier rate, 225 tokens billed at pro tier rate. Burst credits were consumed earlier in the window and do not retroactively change attribution.
```
Ravi: Rust snippet (using reqwest) draft:
```rust
// imports and error handling omitted for brevity
let client = reqwest::Client::new();
let res = client.post("https://api.redwood.com/v1/completions")
  .bearer_auth(&std::env::var("REDWOOD_KEY").unwrap())
  .header("X-Redwood-Client-Tier", "pro") // optional override
  .json(&serde_json::json!({"prompt": "Summarize"}))
  .send().await?;
println!("status: {}", res.status());
```
Zoe: nice. tiny migration note: old header `X-Tier` (pre-v2) -> new `X-Redwood-Client-Tier`. Include a one-line migration bullet so customers searching the docs find it.
Ravi: noted. Also adding a short dashboard caption change: "Quota widget: shows remaining quota, remaining burst credits, and a breakdown of token attribution by tier (default vs override)."
docs-ci-bot: Link check - 1 broken link found in docs/metering.md: /billing/tiers -> 404. Suggested replacement: /pricing/tiers.
Ravi: thanks bot — will fix the link and add a docs-test in docs-tests/ui-anchors that asserts /pricing/tiers resolves after build.
Marta: editorial nits: (1) avoid the word "billed at X rate" — use "attributed to X tier" to avoid legal/price confusion, (2) keep Rust example compact and mark imports omitted, (3) add a changelog line: "Clarified quota tooltip + added Rust SDK snippet (2026-03-20)".
Ravi: done on all three. also added a tiny note for support: "If you see multiple tier rows in the quota window, that's token-level attribution — check for an override header or multi-tenant routing."
Zoe: can you also add a short test in docs-tests that asserts the quota widget copy contains the phrase "computed per token" so we don't regress the wording?
Ravi: adding that assert now — docs-tests/strings/should-mention-token-attribution.js.
OpsBot: Heads-up: recurring support alert created for this doc ambiguity (ticket count 4 in last 30d). If change lands, auto-close the alert after 7 days of zero tickets.
Marta: approving the wording. will do final pass on the Rust snippet.
Zoe: LGTM, small nit removed. Approving PR. :white_check_mark:
Ravi: PR opened: https://git.redwood.com/redwood/docs/pull/1307 — contains tooltip update, Rust/curl/node/python snippets, header migration note, dashboard caption tweak, changelog, and two docs-tests. tagged @Zoe @Marta
Ravi: merging once CI completes. thanks everyone! :rocket:
